THIS CRL.P IS FILED U/S.438 OF CR.P.C TO ENLARGE THE PETITIONER ON BAIL IN THE EVENT OF HIS ARREST IN CR.NO.50/2023 OF GUDIBANDE P.S., CHIKKABALLAPURA DISTRICT FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 406,409,420 R/W 34 OF IPC ON THE FILE OF THE PRINCIPAL CIVIL JUDGE (JR.DN.)
AND J.M.F.C., GUDIBANDE, CHIKKABALLAPURA DISTRICT.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Accused No.1, in Crime No.50/2023 registered by Gudibande Police Station, Chikkaballapura for offences punishable under Sections 406, 409, 420 r/w Section 34 of IPC, is before this Court under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
2.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3. On the complaint of one Sri.Suresh H.G, Regional Manager of Karnataka Gramina Bank, Kolar dated 26.04.2023.
Gudibande Police had registered FIR in Crime No.50/2023 against the petitioner and Sri.Manjunatha Y.N. for the aforesaid offences.

In the complaint, it is alleged that the petitioner was working as Assistant Manager and accused No.2-Manjunatha Y.N. was working as Manager in Yellodu Branch of Karnataka NC: 2023:KHC:29478 Gramina Bank during the period from 08.08.2019 to 24.05.2020.

In the complaint, it is averred that the second accused-Manjunatha Y.N.
had transferred the fixed deposit amount of customer of the bank to the Bank account of the petitioner and the amount found in the savings bank accounts of two other customers was also transferred by the second accused to the bank account of the petitioner.
The alleged fraud was found during internal audit and thereafter, the complainant had approached the jurisdictional Police on 26.04.2023.
Apprehending arrest in the said case, the petitioner had filed Crl.Misc.No.258/2023 before the III Additional District and Sessions Judge, Chikkaballapura, which was dismissed on 23.05.2023.

entities.text: III Additional District and Sessions Judge, Chikkaballapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is under these circumstances, the petitioner is before this Court.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that perusal of the complaint averments itself would go to show that the amount which was transferred to the account of the petitioner was either re-transferred or repaid by the petitioner.

He submits that the allegation of transfer of the amount to the account of the petitioner is on the second accused-Manjunatha NC: 2023:KHC:29478 Y.N and he has been granted anticipatory bail by this Court in Crl.P.No.4534/2023 disposed of on Manindra Reddy S vs State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58275380/
2 22.06.2023.
5.

entities.text: Manindra Reddy S vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned High Court Government Pleader who has opposed the bail application, submits that the amount was transferred to the account of the petitioner by accused No.2 and therefore, he does not stand on the same footing as accused No.2.
6.
From the complaint averments, it is seen that accused No.2 was working as a Manager and the petitioner was working as a Assistant Manager in the Branch Office of Karnataka Gramina Bank.
The allegation in the complaint is that accused No.2 has transferred the amounts to the bank account of the petitioner.
From the perusal of the complaint, it is seen that the amounts which were transferred to the account of the petitioner were either re-transferred or repaid by the petitioner subsequently.
As on the date of filing the complaint, the petitioner has already re-transferred/repaid the amount which was transferred to his account.

Accused No.2, against whom the allegation of transfer of money to the account of the petitioner is made, has been granted anticipatory bail by this NC: 2023:KHC:29478 Court in Crl.P.No.4534/2023 which was disposed of on 22.06.2023.
Under these circumstances, I am of the view that even petitioner is entitled for the relief of anticipatory bail.

Accordingly, following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

In the event of arrest of the petitioner/accused No.2 in Crime No.50/2023 of Gudibande Police Station, he shall be released subject to following conditions:
1. Petitioner shall appear before the Investigation Officer with a period of one week from the date of receipt of a copy of the order and shall execute a bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh Only) with one surety for the likesum.
2. Petitioner shall furnish proof of his address and shall inform the Investigating Officer/Court, if there is any charge in the address.
3. Petitioner shall make himself available for the purpose of investigation as and when required and shall co-operate with the investigation.
Petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the trial Court without prior permission till completion of the investigation of the case.
5. Petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence/witnesses either directly or indirectly.
